question: Public dermatology image datasets with Fitzpatrick/Monk labels and diagnosis, with FST V-VI well represented, for a classifier fairness audit

requirements.text: Skin tone label (Fitzpatrick or Monk) on every image
Fitzpatrick V and VI substantially represented

queries: skin lesion images skin type diagnosis

record.title: Diverse Dermatology Images (DDI)

access.evidence: ddi-dataset.github.io: "By registering for downloads ... you are agreeing to this Research Use Agreement"

record.description: Artificial intelligence (AI) may aid in triaging skin diseases. However, most AI models have not been rigorously assessed on images of diverse skin tones or uncommon diseases. To ascertain potential biases in algorithm performance in this context, we curated the Diverse Dermatology Images (DDI) dataset—the first publicly available, deeply curated, and pathologically confirmed image dataset with diverse skin tones. The DDI was retrospectively selected from reviewing pathology reports in Stanford Clinics from 2010-2020 with further details provided in the methods. After filtering out images that were poor quality (see methods), there were a total of 656 images representing 570 unique patients…

datasets.why: Biopsy-proven diagnoses, 656 images, deliberately balanced across FST; about 207 images are FST V-VI (159 benign, 48 malignant).

R1.evidence: FST I-VI for every image (project site)

R3.evidence: ~207 V-VI images (web search summary of the DDI paper; confirm in metadata)

R4.evidence: register and accept the Research Use Agreement

access_steps: Open the Stanford AIMI / Redivis page and sign in
caveats: Small; wide confidence intervals per subgroup
Non-commercial; no redistribution; do not share download link
Reported: no BCC images in FST V-VI

record.description: The SCIN dataset contains 10,000+ images of dermatology conditions, crowdsourced with informed consent from US internet users. Contributions include self-reported demographic and symptom information and dermatologist labels. The dataset also contains estimated Fitzpatrick skin type and Monk Skin Tone. - google-research-datasets/scin

sentences: The SCIN (Skin Condition Image Network) open access dataset aims to supplement publicly available dermatology datasets from health system sources with representative images from internet users.
To this end, the SCIN dataset was collected from Google Search users in the United States through a voluntary, consented image donation application.
The SCIN Dataset is released under SCIN Data Use License

Assessments of novel crowdsourcing methods to create health datasets are needed.To evaluate if web search advertisements (ads) are effective at creating a diverse and representative dermatology image dataset.This prospective observational survey study, conducted from March to November 2023, used Google Search ads to invite internet users in the US to contri…

datasets.why: Largest set with both FST and Monk labels; but diagnoses are dermatologist differentials, not biopsy.

R1.evidence: Self-reported FST (many NONE_SELECTED), dermatologist-estimated FST and Monk labels; gradable only for some

R2.evidence: Weighted differential labels from 1-3 dermatologists; non-diagnosable cases included

R3.evidence: Paper: eFST5 5.27%, eFST6 0.57%; self-reported FST5 9.84%, FST6 6.57% of ~5,000 cases

R4.evidence: public GCS bucket, SCIN Data Use License

access_steps: Pull scin_cases.csv / scin_labels.csv and images from the dx-scin-public-data bucket (see scin_demo.ipynb)
caveats: eFST VI under 1% means very few reliably dark cases
Self-selected US web users; photos of mixed quality
Licence prohibits re-identification; read it for other limits

papers.title: Creating an Empirical Dermatology Dataset Through Crowdsourcing With Web Search Advertisements

datasets.why: Largest FST-labelled set (16,577 images, 114 conditions), ~2,170 FST V-VI, but labels are noisy.

R1.evidence: FST by Scale AI / Centaur Labs crowd annotators, not dermatologists; ~3% unknown

R2.evidence: Atlas-derived labels, not biopsy; known errors

R4.evidence: CSV is open, images must be downloaded from source atlases (links may rot)

access_steps: Fetch images from the url column, or use the cleaned Fitzpatrick17k-C on Zenodo (CC BY-NC 4.0)
caveats: Skin-tone labels are noisy, which itself affects an audit

papers.title: Investigating the Quality of DermaMNIST and Fitzpatrick17k Dermatological Image Datasets

not_recommended.name: PAD-UFES-20
not_recommended.reason: Has FST but only 10 type V and 1 type VI images of 1,494 labelled.

not_recommended.name: HAM10000 / ISIC archive
not_recommended.reason: No skin-tone labels in the standard release and almost no FST V-VI (as I recall; not checked today).

not_recommended.name: MRA-MIDAS
not_recommended.reason: FST labelled and biopsy-proven, but only 16.8% are III-VI and authors flag few IV-VI.

not_recommended.name: Pipsqueak
not_recommended.reason: All V-VI but only ~16 original images (80 with augmentation), mostly re-taken from Fitzpatrick17k.

not_recommended.name: Black skin acral lesions (Zenodo 10570316)
not_recommended.reason: Access restricted; no FST label stated.

gaps: No large public dataset with biopsy-proven diagnoses and expert FST labels with thousands of V-VI images was found.
Not checked: DDI-2 (Asian patients, V-VI counts unknown), SkinCAP, Fitzpatrick17k-C exact counts.
notes: Redivis page is JavaScript-rendered; DDI access is from the project site. V-VI counts for DDI and Fitzpatrick17k come from secondary summaries.
